scope: CVPR2022 paper pre-training architecture with 75% masking example; pinned official implementation corroborates restoration and masked-only MSE. A 4x4 teaching grid depicts 16 image-patch tokens, four visible and twelve removed; class token is not counted. No training, inference evaluation or performance measurement.
takeaway: High-ratio random masking lets a large encoder process only visible patches; learned mask tokens enter afterward, and a lightweight decoder learns pixel reconstruction with masked-only supervision.

contributionHierarchy.claim: Encode only the visible patch subset; reconstruct the full image with a lightweight decoder
contributionHierarchy.kind: Coupled architectural design, not a new transformer primitive

alternatives.composition: White landscape approximately 1.8:1. Two aligned visual regions: sparse visible-only encoding on the left and restored full-sequence lightweight decoding on the right, linked by the four encoded-visible tokens. Source image-patch grid is upper left, compact masked-only objective is a low supporting strip. Compare token LOAD via four blue encoder tokens versus a 4x4 decoder grid with four blue and twelve gray tokens. No numbered steps, card grid, background bands, oversized overall title or borrowed photographic artwork.
alternatives.mechanism: Alignment and explicit token counts expose encoder/decoder asymmetry. A learned gray-mask-token inlet joins only after the encoder, with Restore order marking the full 4x4 decoder input. A gold dashed mask-metadata path provides restoration indices and the masked-only loss selector; target pixel reference is a thin separate supervision path, never input to the encoder.

alternatives.composition: White landscape approximately 2:1. A continuous left-to-right sparse bottleneck: source patch grid, exactly four visible tokens, large Encoder, exactly four encoded-visible tokens, a post-encoder mask-token merge and full restored 4x4 token grid, then small Lightweight decoder and a 4x4 pixel prediction. The twelve learned mask tokens enter from a short upper branch. Pixel target and masked-only loss occupy a compact lower inset. No two-column panels, numbered card pipeline, background bands or photo assets.
alternatives.mechanism: The narrow visible-token lane through the expensive encoder expands ONLY afterward into the full decoder sequence, making the architectural distinction tangible. Small dashed metadata links carry restoration indices and the same binary mask; original pixel targets feed only supervision. All literal patch tokens and predicted-grid glyphs are schematic, not observed model outputs.
